findings.description: When active_cycle is null the default falls back to the highest-numbered cycle regardless of its status. In the normal post-archive state (the just-archived cycle is the newest and active_cycle was nulled by this very script) a second no-arg run selects an already-archived cycle, passes the completeness gate, re-copies current artifacts over the existing snapshot and rewrites .archived / .archive_path. The command doc's error table still says 'No active cycle' is an error, which the script never emits.
findings.failure_mode: Repeat or scheduled no-arg invocation silently re-archives the previous cycle and overwrites its archived timestamp and snapshot instead of failing with 'No active cycle'.
findings.suggested_fix: In the fallback, restrict to cycles whose .status != "archived" (max of those); if none, print 'No active cycle' and return 1. Alternatively refuse in create_archive when the resolved cycle already has status archived unless --force.

findings.description: The candidate path is passed as a normal git pathspec, so glob magic applies: a directory name containing [ ] * or ? (e.g. a slug like cycle-9-[wip]) is matched as a pattern, not literally, and can yield 'no match' (rc 1) for a tracked directory. Separately, every rc other than 1 (index.lock held by a concurrent git op, corrupt index, pathspec outside tree) is reported as '[WARN] tracked archive kept ... prune it with git', which misdescribes an unverifiable directory as tracked.
findings.failure_mode: A tracked archive dir whose name contains pathspec glob characters is classified untracked and rm -rf'd; transient git errors produce misleading 'tracked' warnings and silently disable pruning for that run.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `git -C "$ARCHIVE_DIR" --literal-pathspecs ls-files --error-unmatch -- "$1"` (or prefix the path with ':(literal)'). Return/print a distinct message for rc >= 2 (e.g. '[WARN] could not verify git status of <path>; kept') so operators are not told to prune with git something git does not track.

findings.description: yq failures (binary missing, YAML parse error) are collapsed into yaml_retention="" with stderr discarded, which is then indistinguishable from 'key absent'. With the new default of 0 this means a configured compound_learning.archive.retention_cycles is silently ignored and the run reports 'retention 0 (default: no --retention, no compound_learning.archive.retention_cycles)', which is false.
findings.failure_mode: Operators who rely on the yaml retention get no pruning and a message asserting the key is not configured; the misconfiguration (missing yq / broken yaml) is never surfaced.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture yq's exit status separately: if `command -v yq` fails or yq exits non-zero on an existing config file, print a [WARN] naming the cause before falling back to keep-all, and set RETENTION_SOURCE to something like 'default (yaml unreadable)' so the dry-run message is accurate.

findings.description: rel_archive_path is derived by a plain prefix strip of "$PROJECT_ROOT"/. If ARCHIVE_DIR is configured outside the repo root, PROJECT_ROOT carries a trailing slash, or the two paths differ by a symlink component, nothing is stripped and an absolute machine-specific path is written into ledger.json as archive_path, contradicting the documented 'relative to the repo root' contract.
findings.failure_mode: Ledger gains a non-portable absolute archive_path that breaks on other checkouts/CI and diverges from the documented schema.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise both sides (e.g. `realpath -m`) and compute with `realpath --relative-to="$PROJECT_ROOT"`; if the result escapes the root (starts with ../ or is absolute) emit a WARN so the operator knows the path is not repo-relative.

findings.description: The check for ledger-lib.sh happens only after the archive directory has been created and populated. When the lib is missing the script prints a WARN and exits 0, leaving an archive on disk whose cycle is still 'active' in the ledger. This both violates the header's 'ledger update failure -> exit 1' contract and defeats the stated goal of checking preconditions 'before any write'.
findings.failure_mode: Broken install (missing ledger-lib.sh) produces an archive/ledger inconsistency while signalling success to callers and automation.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the `[[ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/ledger-lib.sh" ]]` check next to the completeness gate (before mkdir) and treat its absence as a hard error (exit 1) when cycle_id is set, or at minimum exit 1 after the WARN so the inconsistency is not reported as success.

findings.description: The gate counts any sprint whose .status != "completed", so sprints with a missing/null status (older ledgers) and sprints in other terminal states (skipped, cancelled, superseded) all block archiving. The comment claims this mirrors ledger-lib.sh archive_cycle; if that gate treats other terminal states or null differently, the two will disagree and the CLI will refuse cycles the library would archive.
findings.failure_mode: Legacy or partially-skipped cycles become unarchivable without --force, and --force then drops the gate entirely rather than only for the known-terminal states.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the accepted terminal set once (e.g. completed|skipped|cancelled) and treat a missing status as incomplete only when the sprint also lacks a completion marker; ideally source the predicate from ledger-lib.sh so both gates share one definition, and add a test with a null-status sprint.

findings.description: get_current_cycle resolves the exact cycle id (active_cycle or max) but then discards it, emitting only the integer via tonumber (cycle-087 -> 87). create_archive re-derives cycle_id from that number through the pre-existing lookup. If that lookup does not tolerate zero padding or multiple ids sharing a number (cycle-120 and cycle-120-active), the default run silently takes the 'legacy fallback' path: archive named cycle-87, no ledger update. The fixture contains cycle-087 but no test makes it the selected cycle, so this path is unverified.
findings.failure_mode: For zero-padded or duplicated cycle numbers the no-arg run archives to a legacy-named directory and skips the ledger update without error.
findings.suggested_fix: Have get_current_cycle output the resolved id (and let create_archive derive the number from it) rather than the reverse, or add a test where active_cycle is a zero-padded id (cycle-087) and assert 'Cycle id: cycle-087' and the ledger update.
